0.en: Jack pushed through the side door of the hall into a narrow corridor that smelled of floor polish and old coffee. The noise of the crowd dropped to a muffled roar behind him.
0.id: Jack mendorong pintu samping aula dan masuk ke lorong sempit yang berbau semir lantai dan kopi basi. Keriuhan kerumunan meredam menjadi gemuruh teredam di belakangnya.

1.en: Lena. What can you do in ten minutes?
1.id: Lena. Apa yang bisa kamu lakukan dalam sepuluh menit?

2.en: Short of shutting the water off entirely? I can drop the pressure. Block by block. The faucets still run, they just run slowly. Very slowly.
2.id: Selain mematikan air sama sekali? Aku bisa menurunkan tekanannya. Blok demi blok. Kerannya tetap mengalir, cuma pelan. Pelan sekali.

4.en: Filling a bathtub would take most of the morning. Filling a glass would take about as long as it does now if you're patient.
4.id: Mengisi bak mandi bakal makan hampir sepanjang pagi. Mengisi segelas air kira-kira selama sekarang, asal sabar.

5.en: Sarah came through the door behind him, with Doctor Mercer right behind her like a shadow that carried a medical bag.
5.id: Sarah menyusul lewat pintu di belakangnya, dengan Dokter Mercer tepat di belakangnya seperti bayangan yang menenteng tas medis.

6.en: What happens to the people who didn't fill anything yet? The ones who were actually listening to the part about restrictions?
6.id: Lalu bagaimana dengan orang-orang yang belum mengisi apa-apa? Yang benar-benar mendengarkan bagian soal pembatasan?

8.en: They get a slow faucet like everyone else. Nobody gets cut off. Nobody gets ahead any further than they already are.
8.id: Mereka dapat keran pelan seperti semua orang. Tidak ada yang diputus. Tidak ada yang bisa lebih unggul daripada yang sudah-sudah.

9.en: Jack thought about it for the length of one breath.
9.id: Jack memikirkannya selama satu tarikan napas.

10.id: Pertahankan tekanan penuh di bagian medis.

12.en: The kitchens, too. And your station.

13.en: Done. Housing blocks first, then the workshops. Mark's people are going to get calls.
13.id: Beres. Blok hunian dulu, lalu bengkel-bengkel. Orang-orang Mark bakal kebanjiran telepon.

15.en: Every single person in town who was halfway through filling something.
15.id: Dari setiap orang di kota yang sedang setengah jalan mengisi sesuatu.

18.en: Somewhere under the floor, faintly, a pipe knocked as the pressure changed.
18.id: Di suatu tempat di bawah lantai, samar-samar, sebuah pipa berdetak saat tekanannya berubah.

19.en: Mark leaned into the corridor from the hall, his radio already chattering.
19.id: Mark menjulurkan badan ke lorong dari aula, radionya sudah berceloteh.

20.en: Somebody want to tell me why my officers are suddenly getting reports that the water's broken?
20.id: Ada yang mau menjelaskan kenapa petugas-petugasku tiba-tiba dapat laporan bahwa airnya rusak?

21.en: It's not broken. It's slow on purpose.

23.en: Tell them it's slow so there's enough for everybody. Tell them the limits come at noon.
23.id: Bilang saja airnya pelan supaya cukup untuk semua orang. Bilang batasnya diumumkan tengah hari.

24.en: Mark listened to his radio for a moment, then sighed.
24.id: Mark mendengarkan radionya sebentar, lalu mendesah.

25.en: Unit Four says a man in Block C is very upset about his bath.
25.id: Unit Empat bilang ada laki-laki di Blok C yang kesal sekali soal mandinya.

27.en: Tell Unit Four that a man in Block C is going to have the cleanest emergency in the settlement.
27.id: Bilang ke Unit Empat bahwa laki-laki di Blok C itu bakal mengalami keadaan darurat paling bersih di seluruh permukiman.

28.en: Mark turned away and keyed the radio, and Jack heard him say almost exactly that, only more politely.
28.id: Mark berpaling dan menekan tombol radionya, dan Jack mendengarnya mengatakan hal yang nyaris persis sama, hanya lebih sopan.

29.en: Doctor Mercer had waited for all of this with remarkable patience. Now she stepped in front of Jack.
29.id: Dokter Mercer menunggu semua itu dengan kesabaran yang luar biasa. Sekarang ia melangkah ke depan Jack.

31.en: Lena needs me at the utility station.
31.id: Lena butuh saya di stasiun utilitas.

32.en: Lena has your wrist. The utility station has walls. Neither of them is going anywhere. Your hand is bleeding through a rag that has now been through a greenhouse roof and a town meeting.
32.id: Lena punya pergelangan tangan Anda. Stasiun utilitas punya dinding. Tidak satu pun dari keduanya akan ke mana-mana. Tangan Anda berdarah menembus lap yang sekarang sudah melewati atap rumah kaca dan rapat warga.

33.en: Jack looked down. She wasn't wrong. A slow red stain had crept out from under the edge of the cloth.
33.id: Jack menunduk. Dokter Mercer tidak salah. Noda merah perlahan merayap keluar dari bawah tepi kain itu.

35.en: Then it will take very little time to fix.
35.id: Kalau begitu, membereskannya tidak akan makan waktu lama.

36.en: The medical center was a five-minute walk. Doctor Mercer set the pace, and it was fast.
36.id: Pusat medis lima menit jalan kaki. Dokter Mercer yang menentukan langkahnya, dan langkahnya cepat.

37.en: The waiting room was busier than Jack had ever seen it. A man with a sprained wrist. Two older women who had come in together because one of them had fainted on her porch and the other refused to let her come alone. A teenager with a nosebleed who kept apologizing. Every one of them looked up when Jack walked in, and every one of them recognized him.
37.id: Ruang tunggu lebih ramai daripada yang pernah Jack lihat. Seorang laki-laki dengan pergelangan tangan terkilir. Dua perempuan tua yang datang bersama karena salah satunya pingsan di terasnya dan yang satu lagi tidak mau membiarkannya datang sendirian. Seorang remaja mimisan yang terus minta maaf. Setiap orang mendongak ketika Jack masuk, dan setiap orang mengenalinya.

38.en: Nobody said anything. That was almost worse than the hall.
38.id: Tak ada yang berkata apa-apa. Itu nyaris lebih buruk daripada di aula.

39.en: Doctor Mercer steered him into a treatment room and sat him on the edge of a bed. She unwound the rag without ceremony.
39.id: Dokter Mercer menggiringnya ke sebuah ruang perawatan dan mendudukkannya di tepi ranjang. Ia membuka lilitan lap itu tanpa basa-basi.

40.en: The cut ran diagonally across the back of his left hand, shallow at one end and deeper than he would have liked at the other.
40.id: Luka itu melintang miring di punggung tangan kirinya, dangkal di satu ujung dan lebih dalam daripada yang ia harapkan di ujung lainnya.

44.en: She cleaned it, and it stung enough that he stopped talking for a while.
44.id: Ia membersihkannya, dan rasanya cukup perih sampai Jack berhenti bicara untuk sementara.

45.en: Four stitches. Keep it dry. Which, today, should be easy for everyone.
45.id: Empat jahitan. Jaga tetap kering. Yang, hari ini, mestinya gampang untuk semua orang.

46.en: Sarah laughed from the doorway, then tried to turn it into a cough.
46.id: Sarah tertawa dari ambang pintu, lalu berusaha mengubahnya menjadi batuk.

48.en: You're next. Don't think I've forgotten.
48.id: Anda berikutnya. Jangan kira saya lupa.

50.en: The stitches took five minutes. Doctor Mercer worked fast and talked even faster, asking Jack how many hours he had slept, how much he had eaten, and when he had last had water, and making a small disapproving sound at each answer.
50.id: Jahitannya selesai dalam lima menit. Dokter Mercer bekerja cepat dan bicara lebih cepat lagi, menanyai Jack sudah berapa jam ia tidur, sudah makan seberapa banyak, dan kapan terakhir kali minum air, lalu mengeluarkan bunyi kecil tanda tak setuju di setiap jawaban.

51.en: Halfway through the third stitch, Lena's voice came quietly from his wrist.
51.id: Di tengah jahitan ketiga, suara Lena terdengar pelan dari pergelangannya.

52.en: Draw's down to half what it was ten minutes ago. Complaints are up about four times. I'd call that a trade.
52.id: Pemakaian turun sampai separuh dari sepuluh menit lalu. Keluhan naik sekitar empat kali lipat. Kubilang itu tukar-tambah yang lumayan.

56.en: The scanner hummed. A gray shape bloomed on the screen beside the bed, and then the sound came, quick and steady through the speaker, like someone running very lightly on a wooden floor.
56.id: Pemindai berdengung. Sebuah bentuk kelabu merekah di layar di samping ranjang, lalu suara itu datang, cepat dan mantap lewat pengeras suara, seperti seseorang yang berlari sangat ringan di lantai kayu.

57.en: Jack had heard it before. He had heard it a dozen times. It still went straight through him.
57.id: Jack sudah pernah mendengarnya. Sudah belasan kali. Suara itu tetap menembus langsung ke dalam dirinya.

58.en: Sarah let out a breath she had clearly been holding since eleven o'clock the night before.
58.id: Sarah mengembuskan napas yang jelas sudah ia tahan sejak pukul sebelas tadi malam.

60.en: On the screen, the gray shape shifted, and a small knot of shadow pushed outward.
60.id: Di layar, bentuk kelabu itu bergeser, dan segumpal kecil bayangan mendorong ke luar.

63.en: He's been annoyed with me all night. He kicked me during the activation.
63.id: Dia sudah sebal padaku semalaman. Dia menendangku waktu aktivasi.

64.en: Good. A baby who's annoyed is a baby who's paying attention.
64.id: Bagus. Bayi yang sebal adalah bayi yang memperhatikan.

65.en: Doctor Mercer moved the scanner a little higher.
65.id: Dokter Mercer menggeser pemindai sedikit lebih tinggi.

66.en: Heartbeat's strong. Size is right where it should be. Movement's good.
66.id: Detak jantungnya kuat. Ukurannya pas sesuai seharusnya. Gerakannya bagus.

67.en: Jack realized his good hand was gripping the edge of the bed. He let go.
67.id: Jack menyadari tangannya yang tidak terluka sedang mencengkeram tepi ranjang. Ia melepaskannya.

68.en: Then Doctor Mercer wrapped a cuff around Sarah's arm and watched the numbers, and her expression didn't change, which was how Jack knew something had.
68.id: Lalu Dokter Mercer melilitkan manset di lengan Sarah dan memperhatikan angka-angkanya, dan raut wajahnya tidak berubah, dan justru dari situ Jack tahu ada sesuatu yang berubah.

70.en: Your blood pressure's a little high.

71.en: Sarah sat up on her elbows.

73.en: High enough that I'd like to see it lower, and not so high that I'm going to panic about it. You've been on your feet for nine hours in a crisis. I'd be more worried if it were perfect.
73.id: Cukup tinggi sampai saya ingin melihatnya lebih rendah, dan tidak setinggi itu sampai saya harus panik. Anda sudah berdiri selama sembilan jam di tengah krisis. Saya justru lebih khawatir kalau angkanya sempurna.

75.en: So it's a little high. I want you resting. I want you drinking your full share of water. And I want to check it again tonight.
75.id: Jadi agak tinggi. Saya mau Anda istirahat. Saya mau Anda minum jatah air Anda sampai penuh. Dan saya mau memeriksanya lagi nanti malam.

77.id: Di mana saja yang ada kursinya.

78.en: Sarah looked at Jack. Jack, wisely, said nothing at all.
78.id: Sarah memandang Jack. Jack, dengan bijak, tidak berkata apa-apa sama sekali.

79.en: She turned back to Doctor Mercer with the expression she usually saved for conference panels.
79.id: Sarah kembali menghadap Dokter Mercer dengan raut yang biasanya ia simpan untuk panel konferensi.

81.en: The utility station has a crisis.

82.en: Every building in this town has a crisis. At least at the utility station, I can be useful while I sit in one of its chairs.
82.id: Semua bangunan di kota ini sedang krisis. Setidaknya di stasiun utilitas, saya bisa berguna sambil duduk di salah satu kursinya.

83.en: Doctor Mercer looked at her for a long, flat moment. Then she looked at Jack.
83.id: Dokter Mercer menatapnya lama dan datar. Lalu ia menatap Jack.

85.en: Since the day I met her.
85.id: Sejak hari pertama saya bertemu dengannya.

86.en: Fine. Mark drives you. You sit. You do not climb anything, carry anything, or argue with anyone for more than five minutes at a time. If you feel a headache, dizziness, anything strange with your vision, you call me. Not him. Me.
86.id: Baiklah. Mark yang mengantar Anda. Anda duduk. Anda tidak memanjat apa pun, tidak mengangkat apa pun, dan tidak berdebat dengan siapa pun lebih dari lima menit sekali debat. Kalau Anda merasa sakit kepala, pusing, ada yang aneh dengan penglihatan Anda, Anda telepon saya. Bukan dia. Saya.

89.en: Doctor Mercer pulled the cuff off Sarah's arm and shook her head, but Jack could have sworn the corner of her mouth moved.
89.id: Dokter Mercer melepas manset dari lengan Sarah dan menggeleng, tapi Jack berani bersumpah sudut bibirnya bergerak.

90.en: Mark was waiting outside with the vehicle running. Jack helped Sarah into the back seat, and for once she let him.
90.id: Mark sudah menunggu di luar dengan mesin kendaraan menyala. Jack membantu Sarah naik ke kursi belakang, dan kali ini Sarah membiarkannya.

91.en: Lena's voice came through his wrist as they pulled away.
91.id: Suara Lena terdengar dari pergelangannya saat mereka melaju pergi.

92.en: Draw curve's flattening. You'll want to see this in person. I'm heading to the station now. The gauges there are older than the sensors, and I trust them more.
92.id: Kurva pemakaian mulai mendatar. Kamu pasti mau melihat ini langsung. Aku berangkat ke stasiun sekarang. Alat ukur di sana lebih tua daripada sensornya, dan aku lebih percaya alat ukur itu.

94.en: Good. There's something else you should know before you get here.
94.id: Bagus. Ada hal lain yang perlu kamu tahu sebelum sampai.

96.en: The machine shop's water was shut off last night with the rest of the industrial lines. Somebody just noticed.
96.id: Air di bengkel mesin dimatikan semalam bersama jalur industri lainnya. Barusan ada yang sadar.

99.en: They turned the last corner, and the utility station came into view, a squat concrete building with tall pipes running along one side. A small knot of people stood outside its door. In the middle of them, broad and gray-bearded and very much awake, Paul Harlan stood with his arms folded, arguing with a man in a technician's jacket who looked like he would have paid good money to be somewhere else.
99.id: Mereka berbelok di tikungan terakhir, dan stasiun utilitas mulai terlihat, sebuah bangunan beton pendek dan gempal dengan pipa-pipa tinggi berjajar di satu sisinya. Sekelompok kecil orang berdiri di depan pintunya. Di tengah-tengah mereka, bertubuh lebar dan berjanggut kelabu dan sangat terjaga, Paul Harlan berdiri bersedekap, berdebat dengan seorang laki-laki berjaket teknisi yang tampaknya rela membayar mahal untuk berada di tempat lain.

100.en: Paul saw the vehicle, and stopped arguing, and waited.
100.id: Paul melihat kendaraan itu, berhenti berdebat, dan menunggu.

101.en: Sarah sighed from the back seat.

102.en: Five minutes. I'm allowed to argue for five minutes.
102.id: Lima menit. Aku boleh berdebat lima menit.
